newsitem.title: USA: U.S. health officials study anti-AIDS drug.
newsitem.headline: U.S. health officials study anti-AIDS drug.

text.p: The drug AZT remains the best way to prevent an AIDS-infected pregnant woman from passing the virus onto her unborn child, despite some studies on mice that suggest a possible risk of eventual cancer in the children, medical experts said on Tuesday.
The panel of experts convened by the National Institutes of Health said more research is needed into the possible AZT cancer link and that children exposed to it in utero should be carefully tracked.

And pregnant women considering AZT, or Zidovudine, treatment to avoid perinatal transmission should be informed of the possible risks, the experts agreed at the end of a day of meetings reviewing the research. A formal statement on their conclusions will be completed in a few days.
So far, there have been no cases of cancer in children linked to AZT, although since the drug has only been used widely for a few years it could be too early to detect a problem.
